description:
Extends fsck from 'each chunk is well-formed' to 'each chunk holds what it should'.

The authoritative shard layout is not in object storage. It lives in the keyspace family \xFF/system/shard_keys/<end_key> -> {tag, start_key}, which is itself materialized from chunks. So fsck has a bootstrap step: replay shard 0 to recover the shard map, then validate everything else against it.

Checks:
- The recovered shard_keys/ family is gapless and non-overlapping from "" through end.
- Every mutation in every slice falls inside the key range of the shard whose prefix it was stored under. This is the real shard-coverage check for the shard-centric storage work (bedrock-q67).
- Shard tags referenced in the layout have corresponding c/ prefixes, and vice versa.

Reuse the SystemKeys reader for decoding shard_keys entries and Transaction.mutations/1 for slice contents. Depends on the chunk decoding from the first fsck slice.
title: fsck: shard layout recovery and key-range containment
